findings.title: Deletion receipt overclaims: 'removed' names sinks that were not removed, and derived_consolidations counts the deleted record's own rows
findings.recommendation: At deletion_sinks, report a derived or cached row in 'removed' only when this call removed or rekeyed it; otherwise move it to 'pending' (the receipt already carries that list and MemoryDeletionError consumes it at lifecycle.rb:93). Exclude the deleted key's own versions from the LIKE self-match. No new deletion machinery.

findings.title: No production caller deletes a memory and no retention pass is scheduled, so deleted plaintext persists and memory grows without bound
findings.recommendation: Schedule the pass that already exists: invoke MemoryStore#purge_expired from the worker's existing maintenance/sweep seam (where the toolbox stale-staging sweep runs). Separately make Lifecycle#delete tombstone the store head so the h.deleted = 1 branch is reachable; append already accepts deleted: (store.rb:65) and IndexRow#state already carries 'deleted', so this is one flag at lifecycle.rb:156. Confirm maintenance-pass ownership with the worker_runtime.rb owner first.

findings.title: The behavior-transition crash-recovery path release_or_finalize has no production caller, so a crash between claim and finalize wedges the registry
findings.recommendation: At the existing first-intake seam (session_bindings.rb:23, immediately before claim_behavior_transition), call release_or_finalize for the observed pending_transition_id using the session-store reader as the session_references lambda. No recovery daemon. Route to the tamoz-agent-session row.

findings.title: Every negative admission outcome on the session path is swallowed; AdmissionResult#stored? from the 089 fix has no production consumer
findings.recommendation: At the existing session_memory.rb:92 rescue, log AdmissionResult#reason and #stored? through the logger the session already holds and count them on the existing memory-summary projection (worker_runtime.rb:908). No new signal catalog entries.

findings.title: cas_control ignores its expected argument and CASes against a re-read version, widening the control-record window beyond the caller's validated read
findings.recommendation: Pass the caller's expected through to if_version: and delete the internal re-read, so the fail-closed behaviour the surrounding comments claim is the behaviour that runs.

tests_not_run.reason: time budget; admission assertions overlap the tamoz-stream row more than F19's

confirmed_sound: admission cannot be steered by untrusted content on any of the three gates; :observed requires the authenticated reconciled-outcome reference and the bare independently_observed boolean has no power
the consolidation model call is routed through EffectDispatcher.run with a deterministic logical key (consolidation.rb:194-210); no raw model call inside a node — no FX violation
retrieval is scoped correctly: no cross-thread, cross-user, or cross-project leak; superseded and deleted versions leave active recall via the head-join
bounds are declared and enforced for statement bytes, source refs, lexical hits, token budget, injection count, consolidation batch, and query terms
blind_spots: purge_expired was read and grepped but not executed, so its still_pending list shape on a real tombstone set is a lead, not a finding
F19-REL-01 rests on a repo-wide grep for release_or_finalize by name; a dynamic dispatch or eval surface would not be found
Consolidation#consolidate also has no production caller; not raised separately because no source comment claims a scheduled caller for it, unlike the retention pass
tamoz-evals-runner MemoryRepositoryAdapter builds a second engine over the same store; its treatment paths were not traced
deletion of :sensitive records was not probed (probes used :internal records with no protection codec)
coordinator_flags: needs independent challenge — F19-SEC-01 rests on a synthetic derived record rather than the consolidation pipeline
F19-DEL-01 and F19-REL-01 both bottom out in missing callers owned by other rows (worker_runtime maintenance pass; tamoz-agent-session recovery seam) — route before recording a fix
F19-OBS-01 is the carried-forward residual of top-100 089, not a new defect in admission.rb
possible duplicate of F07-REL-01 only in the 'unreachable pass' shape; the seams are unrelated (SQLite inbox claimer vs memory retention)
